seasons.title: FAO / 11th World Forestry Congress: Safed musli, a wonder drug in the tropical zone
seasons.quote: Being a Kharif crop, the sowing of mush starts with the first shower of the monsoons.

days_to_first_harvest.title: Indian Horticulture (ICAR), Sept-Oct 2023: Production technology of safed musli
days_to_first_harvest.quote: The roots should be harvested carefully by digging from December to January
days_to_first_harvest.note: Planted at the first or second monsoon rain (mid-June to July), dug in December-January: about 180 days. Agronomist to confirm.

harvest_span_days.title: Indian Horticulture (ICAR), Sept-Oct 2023: Production technology of safed musli
harvest_span_days.quote: The roots should be harvested carefully by digging from December to January
harvest_span_days.note: December to January: about 30 days of digging.

spacing_row_cm.title: Indian Horticulture (ICAR), Sept-Oct 2023: Production technology of safed musli
spacing_row_cm.quote: Mostly spacing should be kept about 30 cm row-to-row and 10 or 15 cm plant-to-plant

spacing_plant_cm.title: Indian Horticulture (ICAR), Sept-Oct 2023: Production technology of safed musli
spacing_plant_cm.quote: Mostly spacing should be kept about 30 cm row-to-row and 10 or 15 cm plant-to-plant

water_need.title: Indian Horticulture (ICAR), Sept-Oct 2023: Production technology of safed musli
water_need.quote: Safed musli has short stature, low water requirement
water_need.note: Needs 6-8 irrigations at 10-15 day intervals if the monsoon fails.

waterlogging_tolerant.title: Indian Horticulture (ICAR), Sept-Oct 2023: Production technology of safed musli
waterlogging_tolerant.quote: care should be taken to provide proper drainage to avoid damage to tubers by waterlogging

expected_yield_kg_per_sqm.title: Indian Horticulture (ICAR), Sept-Oct 2023: Production technology of safed musli
expected_yield_kg_per_sqm.quote: This yield gives about 0.4-0.6 tonne marketable dry root yield.
expected_yield_kg_per_sqm.note: 0.4 t/ha = 0.04 kg/m² of dry peeled roots (lowest figure).

economics.title: Indian Horticulture (ICAR), Sept-Oct 2023: Production technology of safed musli
economics.quote: The roots fetch an attractive market price of ` 1600-1800 per kg of dry peeled fasciculated roots.
economics.note: Price quoted in a 2023 article, not a mandi record. Wild collection is why the species is threatened; the market for cultivated roots is thin, so confirm a buyer first.

economics.title: Indian Horticulture (ICAR), Sept-Oct 2023: Production technology of safed musli
economics.quote: planting material (roots) is required and the planting material rate varies with the spacing followed
economics.note: 600 to 1000 kg of planting roots per hectare is the main cost.

source_notes: AI research batch 15 (2026-10-08), medicinal and ayurvedic crops. Ranges are stored at their lower bound; the source range is in each quote. Yields are of the dried product that is sold (dried root, leaf or seed) unless a note says fresh. Sowing dates are from national guides (region india) unless a Malwa study is named. Medicinal crops are planned only when the owner picks the medicinal method; the market for each is thin and buy-back is not assured (see the economics sources).

sow_windows.title: Indian Horticulture (ICAR), Sept-Oct 2023: Production technology of safed musli
sow_windows.quote: The planting should be done on rainy days preferably the first or second rain of monsoon arrival
sow_windows.note: Monsoon reaches Malwa in mid-to-late June: dates are an interpretation. Agronomist to confirm.
